# Bureau

> Bureau is a free compound interest calculator at https://bureau.money. Enter a starting balance, interest rate, time period and regular contributions to see how savings or investments grow, with a year-by-year chart and table. No sign-up required.

Bureau has a UK edition (GBP, ISAs, UK tax) and a US edition (USD, 401(k)/IRA, US tax). Results can be shown in 10 currencies: GBP, USD, EUR, INR, BRL, SGD, MXN, JPY, CAD and AUD.

The calculator supports:

- Initial investment, annual interest rate and duration (years and months)
- Compounding weekly, monthly or yearly
- Regular contributions (weekly, monthly or yearly), made at the start or end of each period, with optional yearly growth in the contribution amount
- Regular withdrawals
- Annual management fees
- Inflation adjustment (shows results in today's money)
- Tax on interest above a tax-free amount

Bureau is for informational purposes only and is not financial advice.

## Pages

- [Compound interest calculator (UK)](https://bureau.money): Calculator in GBP, with FAQs on ISAs, UK tax on interest, the Rule of 72 and choosing a rate of return
- [Compound interest calculator (US)](https://bureau.money/us): Calculator in USD, with FAQs on 401(k)s, IRAs and US tax on interest
- [Mortgage calculator](https://bureau.money/mortgage-calculator): UK mortgage repayments, total interest, loan to value and the effect of overpaying, for repayment and interest-only mortgages. Link a pre-filled calculation with `p` (price), `d` (deposit), `r` (rate %), `t` (term in years), `type` (`rep` or `io`) and `op` (monthly overpayment)
- [Mortgage overpayment calculator](https://bureau.money/mortgage-overpayment-calculator): How much interest and time monthly overpayments save on a UK mortgage
- [Loan and car finance calculator](https://bureau.money/loan-calculator): Monthly repayments and total interest for personal loans and hire purchase car finance, at any APR
- [Pension calculator](https://bureau.money/pension-calculator): UK pension pot at retirement, with employer contributions, basic-rate tax relief, fees, inflation and the 25% tax-free lump sum
- [£250,000 mortgage repayments](https://bureau.money/mortgage-calculator/250000-mortgage): Monthly payments on a £250,000 mortgage at different rates and terms
- [£15,000 loan repayments](https://bureau.money/loan-calculator/15000-loan): Monthly payments and interest on a £15,000 loan over 2 to 7 years
- [£200 a month into a pension](https://bureau.money/pension-calculator/200-a-month): What £200 a month into a UK pension grows to, by starting age
- [Income from a £500,000 pension](https://bureau.money/pension-calculator/500000-pot): How much monthly income a £500,000 UK pension pot could pay, with or without 25% tax-free cash. The pension calculator also has a retirement income mode (`mode=income`)
- [ISA calculator](https://bureau.money/isa-calculator): How an ISA could grow with regular contributions, with the 2026/27 allowance and the April 2027 cash ISA change
- [How much will £10,000 grow?](https://bureau.money/how-much-will-10000-grow): What £10,000 grows to at different rates and timeframes, with or without monthly top-ups

## Linking to a pre-filled calculation

Any calculation can be linked with query parameters, so a reader opens the calculator with the numbers already entered. Parameters that are left out use the defaults (1,000 in the page's currency at 5% for 5 years, compounded monthly).

- `i`: initial investment (number)
- `r`: annual interest rate, % (number)
- `cf`: compounding frequency: `w` weekly, `m` monthly, `y` yearly
- `dy`: duration in years; `dm`: extra months
- `ap`: regular contribution amount; `apf`: its frequency (`w`, `m`, `y`)
- `das`: `1` if contributions are made at the start of each period
- `dg`: yearly growth in contributions, %
- `wd`: regular withdrawal amount; `wf`: its frequency (`w`, `m`, `y`)
- `mf`: annual management fee, %
- `inf`: `1` to adjust for inflation; `ir`: inflation rate, %
- `tfa`: tax-free amount; `tr`: tax rate, %
- `cur`: currency code (for example `GBP`, `USD`, `EUR`)

Example: £10,000 plus £200 a month at 7% for 20 years:
https://bureau.money/?i=10000&r=7&dy=20&ap=200
